description: Four independent curve generators sharing one time base, each with its own end-of-cycle trigger, and a running sum and trigger stream taken from whichever of them are not patched out

params.text: Cycles the shape of that segment through up, down, up-down, down-up and a held constant; the lamp reads red, green, orange, blue and white in that order
Sets how long that segment takes, as a multiplier on the module's time scale: a quarter at the far left, one at centre and sixteen times at the far right
Sets how much of the segment is played before it stops, all of it at the far right and a shorter fragment as it is turned down; the fragment takes the whole time set for the segment
Sets how many triggers are spread through that segment, 1 to 8
Bends the shape of that segment away from straight lines, symmetrical at centre; for the held constant shape this knob sets the value that is held instead
Chooses how the triggers are spread through a segment: down, they are spaced evenly in time; up, they are spaced evenly up the segment's height, so a steep part fires them faster
Scales the height of that segment, silent at the far left, unity at centre and double at the far right
Sets the time every segment is measured against, 64 milliseconds at the far left to about a second at the far right

inputs.text: Starts that segment from the beginning; it fires on any rise in voltage
A trigger here resets the running output to zero and stops all four segments

outputs.text: A 10V pulse the moment that segment finishes, whether it ran to its end or stopped short
That segment's own curve, five volts at full height and scaled by its amp knob; patching this jack takes the segment out of the module's running and trig outputs
The running total of every segment not patched out at its own jack, held between -10V and 10V; it sums their movements rather than their values, so it drifts and stays where it is left
A 10V pulse whenever any segment that is not patched out at its own jack fires one of its triggers

notes: Nothing moves until a trigger arrives at a segment's own trig jack; the segments do not free-run and the reset jack only stops them
The module declares a scaled sum output that has no jack on the panel, so the running output is the only summed voltage available
